object_context: Whole-space Type-I Navier-Stokes blow-up-classification sibling. Test whether the already registered finite-I magnitude ledger A+C+D+E plus the suitable local-energy inequality and pressure localization can itself furnish a signed temporal/no-recrossing law, or whether a new signed flux/correlation coordinate and additional trajectory/global input are required. Type-II remains out of scope.
structural_coordinates: parabolic scaling u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t)
finite I controls nonnegative scale-invariant magnitudes A,C,D,E but does not encode the sign of mixed local-energy flux terms
the local-energy inequality contains signed transport/pressure work through (|u|^2+2p)u·grad(phi), in addition to cutoff/time/diffusion terms
spatial-mean pressure normalization is compatible with divergence-free local-energy testing; the active issue is correlation/sign, not pressure gauge
local pressure decomposes into a localized Calderon-Zygmund contribution plus a harmonic/nonlocal remainder; local pressure representation does not eliminate far-field/gluing obligations
strong L3_loc velocity and weak L3/2_loc pressure compactness are insufficient by themselves to pass a sign-definite global tail/no-recrossing statement

a pressure-free exact smooth shear solution can display inward local kinetic-energy replenishment; it is a hostile local-PDE calibration only and is not a finite-energy/finite-I ancient Clay-class witness
Albritton-Barker ancient Liouville requires a separate global L3 backward-sequence hypothesis; an epsilon-regularity criterion or pressure representation theorem is not an ancient Liouville theorem
same-context expert review supplies no independent mathematical review credit
Type-II remains a separate open sibling even if this Type-I atom closes

target_interface.producer_input: mild bounded ancient Type-I Navier-Stokes solution with finite registered I, or the pre-singularity suitable sequence producing it
target_interface.existing_state: A,C,D,E magnitude bounds; suitable local-energy inequality; local pressure decomposition; local compactness
target_interface.desired_output: a scale-critical signed potential/increment/flux certificate with one-sided temporal behavior strong enough to prevent repeated critical threshold recrossing or to activate an exact source-valid rigidity theorem
target_interface.audit_question: Does the existing state already encode the required sign/temporal orientation, or is a separately controlled signed correlation/flux coordinate necessary?

solved_analogues.fact: Type-I singularity is tied to a nontrivial mild bounded ancient finite-I solution; global-L3-on-a-backward-sequence is a separate Liouville trigger.
local pressure can be reformulated using local Leray projection in regularity theory; this is representation/local regularity machinery, not a no-recrossing theorem.
signed head-pressure distributions can capture pressure oscillation in epsilon-regularity criteria; conditional regularity does not supply temporal monotonicity for the finite-I ancient class.

explicit_disanalogies: Failure of absolute shell bookkeeping does not imply failure of a signed telescoping law.
A pressure-free local-suitable calibration is not a counterexample to a finite-I ancient theorem.
Pressure epsilon-regularity and local pressure projection are not ancient-solution rigidity.
Local sign information does not automatically glue to global L3 tail tightness or backward-uniqueness hypotheses.
A Type-I result does not close Type-II.

counterexample_first_falsifier.model: u(x,t)=(f(x2,t),0,0), p=0 with f_t=f_x2x2. Choose smooth nonnegative f0 supported outside [-R,R]; the heat kernel makes f(y,t)>0 in [-R,R] for t>0, so kinetic energy in B_R rises from zero despite zero pressure.
counterexample_first_falsifier.verification_scope: exact smooth Navier-Stokes/local-energy solution and sign calibration
counterexample_first_falsifier.difference_witness: independent of x1,x3, hence not global finite energy and not asserted finite-I/ancient; it can falsify only pressure-alone/local-identity one-sidedness, not a finite-I dynamics-specific theorem
